evidence: Five rounds. 99 candidates hunting unstudied problems, two large-market probes, and four market-timed candidates under preregistration 0004. Zero selected in every round.

finding_1.claim: Large buyer implies crowded. The hole exists where the money is not.
finding_1.evidence: Carved-DEFLATE has a hole because forensic fragment attribution is a small market. Every large-market probe closed: speech source tracing has MLAAD, DiffSSD, STOPA and an Interspeech special session; video parameter recovery has 98.88% CRF prediction and an H.264 fragment-parameter paper; LLM provenance has a survey, which means the field is mature.

finding_2.claim: The timing window is SHORTER than the time it takes to observe it.
finding_2.consequence: TIMING IS NOT AN EDGE FOR A SOLO FOUNDER. It only looks like one in hindsight.
finding_2.evidence: Post-quantum cryptography is the cleanest case. NIST finalised FIPS 203/204/205 on 2024-08-13. Within 24 months: two USPTO patents specifically on CBOM generation from binary executables, a benchmark (CREBench), a conference paper, and three funded commercial products - IBM Quantum Safe Explorer, SandboxAQ AQtive Guard, Keyfactor, which acquired InfoSec Global in 2025 for exactly this. The market was dateable and the field had already moved.
finding_2.mechanism: A market event is PUBLIC INFORMATION, SYMMETRIC TO EVERYONE. Regulations are announced years ahead. Standards processes are public. Everyone receives the same signal at the same time, and the well-capitalised receive it first because they employ people whose job is to watch. By the time an event is citable, you are already late.

finding_3.access: The founder has no proprietary corpus. Closed.
finding_3.capability: Open in principle, but requires a technical edge over well-funded teams.
finding_3.claim: That leaves ACCESS and CAPABILITY - and a fourth that the FDM-1 story is usually misread as excluding.
finding_3.the_fourth: EFFORT. FDM-1's moat was probably not information and not capability. VPT was published in 2022. Screen recordings were not a secret. Inverse dynamics models were textbook. What nobody wanted to do was build an 11-million-hour pseudo-labelling pipeline. The barrier was WILLINGNESS TO DO AN EXPENSIVE, UNGLAMOROUS, INDUSTRIAL-SCALE DATA JOB THAT WAS FULLY VISIBLE TO EVERYONE.
finding_3.why_it_matters: This is the only escape a solo founder with no data and no capital actually controls, and it is the one the search was never aimed at. Rounds 1-4 hunted information edges - unstudied problems - and lost every time, because information is the thing a solo founder is worst positioned to have.

honest_limits: Four candidates is not a market survey. The finding that timing is closed rests on one clean case (post-quantum) and three weaker ones.
The claim that FDM-1's moat was effort rather than information is an INTERPRETATION of a public story, not a measurement. It is not verifiable from here and is labelled as interpretation.
This is a screen, not an experiment. Nothing here has been measured.
the_bind_restated: An effort edge is bounded by what others will out-spend. Large market implies a funded player will out-effort you. Small market implies you can win but the prize is small. The only target that escapes both is a LARGE market where the required effort is DISPROPORTIONATE TO THE APPARENT PAYOFF, so funded players do not bother. That is a much narrower and much better-specified thing to look for than 'white space', and it is what a sixth round should hunt if there is one.
title: Why the timing escape is closed for a solo founder, and what is left
